title: Small Bottle, Big Pipe: Quantifying and Addressing the Impact of Data Centers on Public Water Systems
authors: Yuelin Han; Pengfei Li; Adam Wierman; Shaolei Ren

methods: Cooling-demand growth scenarios linked to public water capacity; revision incorporates EPA surplus-treatment-capacity statistics.
finding: Peak withdrawals create infrastructure needs poorly represented by annual totals.
limitations: Assumption-sensitive projections; local utilities require measured load profiles.

title: Locational Marginal Emissions for Carbon-Aware Data Center Operations in Large-Scale Power Grids
type: Preprint; peer review and final publication not verified
methods: Hourly dispatch simulation on a 1,493-bus network, evaluating operations, siting and procurement.
finding: Nodal marginal signals help evaluate system emissions changes under modeled interventions.
limitations: Uses historical load/weather inputs and modeled grid dispatch; does not establish real-world causal reductions.
access: Author archive abstract, version history and full HTML verified.

title: ITU-T L.1410 (11/2024): Methodology for environmental life cycle assessments of information and communication technology goods, networks and services
authors: International Telecommunication Union, Telecommunication Standardization Sector
methods: ICT life-cycle assessment and comparison with a reference system, including functional units, shared-process allocation, uncertainty and sensitivity.

title: AP-42, Volume I, Chapter 3: Stationary Internal Combustion Sources
theme: generators; NOx; particulate matter; emission estimation
methods: Equipment- and fuel-specific emission factors for stationary engines and turbines; factors estimate pollutant mass from activity.
finding: Engine characteristics and operation matter for estimating emissions; emitted mass does not itself establish nearby concentrations or observed health outcomes.
limitations: Factors are estimates rather than campus emissions measurements. Appropriate equipment categories, controls and factor uncertainty must be checked; dispersion and health modeling require additional methods and data.
access: EPA current chapter page and linked section 3.4 April 2025 PDF retrieved.

title: ISO 1996-1:2016: Acoustics — Description, measurement and assessment of environmental noise — Part 1: Basic quantities and assessment procedures
type: Primary international standard; public abstract reviewed
methods: Defines environmental-noise quantities and assessment procedures with attention to impulsiveness, tonality and low-frequency content.
finding: Noise assessment needs specified physical quantities and sound characteristics; this standard does not set universal environmental-noise limits.
limitations: Public abstract, not licensed full standard, was reviewed. Detailed instrument protocols and applicable local limits must be obtained for a site study. Framework cadence is an analyst recommendation.
access: ISO public abstract and status page read; page states reviewed and confirmed in 2021.

title: NPDES Permit Writers’ Manual: Chapter 8, Monitoring and Reporting Conditions
methods: Explains representative locations, sampling methods, analytical methods and frequency selection for effluent monitoring and reporting.
finding: Flow and pollutant characteristics require representative measurement; sampling frequency depends on discharge variability and receiving conditions.
limitations: General methodology is not a determination that a particular campus needs a particular permit. Current facility permits and relevant authority decisions govern applicable limits and reporting.
access: Full 15-page chapter retrieved through current EPA manual landing page.

title: Guidance Note 6: Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Management of Living Natural Resources
venue: IFC Guidance Note 6; January 2012, updated June 2019
methods: Project scoping, biodiversity baselines, field surveys, community consultation and monitoring across relevant habitat and infrastructure boundaries.
finding: Area alone cannot characterize ecological impacts; assess affected habitats and ecosystem services against an appropriate baseline.
limitations: Used as an assessment reference, not a claim of a U.S. legal requirement or compliance with IFC standards. No site habitat observations extracted.
access: Official current PS6 page and linked 49-page Guidance Note 6 retrieved; baseline and impact-identification sections read.

title: Data Centers
methods: Agency explanation of demand forecasting, building benchmarking, thermal generation jurisdiction and SPPE review.
finding: CEC uses utility application information for demand forecasts and benchmarks covered buildings. CEC reviews qualifying onsite thermal generation while local agencies permit the data center.
limitations: Forecast applications are not realized load. An exemption from CEC licensing is not an exemption from CEQA review or other required permits.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: AB 1577: Data centers: reporting
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Establishes CEC operator reporting for data centers with electrical capacity at least 10 MW, local estimated energy/noise disclosures, public anonymized aggregation, and IEPR assessments from 2029.
limitations: Ordinary statute effective January 1, 2027; CEC determines submission timing. Specified public, research and utility facilities are excluded. No per-model AI environmental reporting requirement.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: AB 2383: Electricity: data centers
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Requires transmission/distribution and generation tariffs, protection from incremental generation costs, at least ten-year payment mechanisms, and CCA/provider generation tariffs by January 1, 2028.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2027; requires implementing decisions. Generation tariff thresholds must not exceed 25 MW and specified exemptions apply to generation provisions, not necessarily every tariff.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: AB 2469: Data centers: water use disclosures
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Conditions construction and peak-water-increasing expansion approvals on water assessment, projected use, efficiency/workforce disclosures and funding necessary water infrastructure; scarcity plan requirement starts January 1, 2028.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2027 except later specified scarcity-plan date; no MW threshold. Meeting conditions does not compel approval or establish hydrological sustainability.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: AB 2619: Water resources: data centers
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Requires initial-license water estimates, supplier notice, renewal water-use reporting including source and cooling type, and inclusion of unconstrained large-user demand in supplier shortage planning.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2027. Includes data centers below 2 MW. Direct annual water use covers onsite withdrawals/deliveries, not exclusively evaporative consumption.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: SB 886: California Technology Innovation and Ratepayer Protection Act
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Requires CPUC tariffs/rules by January 1, 2028; transmission interconnection provisions address project duplication, upgrade costs, refunds, termination and geographic interconnection information.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2027; transmission provisions cover new agreements from that date. Federal law constrains transmission allocation; definitions are supplied by companion AB 2383.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: SB 887: CEQA, environmental leadership development projects and data centers
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Addresses CEQA applicability and categorical exemptions and creates a conditional route for data centers to qualify as environmental leadership development projects.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2027; facility exceptions and project certification matter. Hourly zero-carbon, storage, water and community-benefit conditions govern this streamlining route, not all existing facilities.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: SB 1168: Data centers: rate structures
methods: Direct review of chaptered text, Legislative Counsel's digest, definitions, operative provisions and approval date.
finding: Directs CPUC to assess rates that assign reasonable transmission/distribution costs and proportionate procurement costs to data centers and relieve residential rate pressure.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2027; directs assessment in a new or existing proceeding. It does not itself promulgate a rate schedule or numerical allocation.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: SB 57: Electrical corporations: data centers: report
methods: Chaptered text reviewed for authorization, reporting deadline and sunset.
finding: CPUC may assess cost shifts from data-center load, procurement and network investment; a completed assessment must be submitted and posted by January 1, 2027.
limitations: Effective January 1, 2026, with January 1, 2031 sunset. The act authorizes an assessment and does not mandate a new data-center tariff.
access: Official primary source; publicly accessible; reviewed 2026-10-01

title: Annual Water Supply and Demand Assessment
methods: Agency explanation of Water Code §10632.1 annual assessments, shortage responses and Bulletin 161.
finding: Covered urban suppliers assess supply-demand balance and report shortages annually from 2022, generally by July 1. Reports support near-term drought response alongside UWMP and shortage-contingency planning.
limitations: Supplier-level planning does not guarantee water availability for a specific facility. Imported-water allocation timing creates a specified deadline exception; actual conditions need ongoing reassessment.
